::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Codebase operators only.** Every clip on this page is produced by a *registered core
operator* run through the Plexus engine — one `config/**.yaml` spec, no per-simulation code.
The interaction and boids laws are ported from
[ParticleGraph](https://github.com/allierc/ParticleGraph); the slime-mould (Physarum) agent
from [Sebastian Lague's Slime-Simulation](https://github.com/SebLague/Slime-Simulation); the
softened self-gravity from Philip Mocz's *Create Your Own N-body Simulation* (2020); the
continuum solver is MLS-MPM (Hu et al. 2018); and each strange attractor cites its originating
paper (Lorenz 1963, Rössler 1976, Sprott 1994, …). Prototype-only experiments have been
dropped — the gallery is the live operator vocabulary of the paper.
:::

Each clip below is one `spec.yaml` over the identical operators and schedule grammar;
**hover (or tab to) a simulation's title to read the exact spec that generated it.** The
first two are validated to floating-point precision against
[ParticleGraph](https://github.com/allierc/ParticleGraph). Every movie is rendered the same
way: a black-background, full-frame point splat, so the *dynamics* — not the chrome — is what
you compare across systems.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## How a clip is made
`python Plexus_Main.py -o generate_plot <config>` runs the forward simulation, writes the
trajectory, and renders the movie — no per-simulation code, only the spec differs. e.g.
`... -o generate_plot inverse_square/spiral_galaxy_3d` or `... -o generate_plot attractors/lorenz`.
:::

```{=html}

<h2>Stigmergy — Physarum slime</h2>
<p class="opk">A set + a scalar field, coupled: agents deposit a trail, the field diffuses and decays, agents sense and steer up it — a self-reinforcing transport network.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery">
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/slime.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>
      <span class="sim-name" tabindex="0">slime<span class="sim-spec"><pre>ops: deposit + diffuse + decay + sense + glide
# 3-sensor steering up a self-deposited pheromone
# field (Jones/Lague). Stigmergy: network grows,
# coarsens, and prunes.
config/slime/slime_default.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">deposit → diffuse → decay → sense → glide — a growing, coarsening web</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

<h2>Continuum mechanics — MLS-MPM</h2>
<p class="opk">The same particle Level, now a material: the decomposed MLS-MPM cycle (strain → scatter → grid solve → gather) carries elastic, fluid, and granular bodies.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery">
  <figure class="sim-card">
    <video src="gallery/material.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline preload="metadata"></video>
    <figcaption>

     -> mpm_gather   (MLS-MPM substep cycle)
# three neo-Hookean elastic balls dropped in a 3D
# box; grid solve handles contact + gravity.
config/material/material_3d_balls_bouncy.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">MLS-MPM continuum — three elastic balls collide and bounce in 3D</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

<h2>Inverse-square law — self-gravity &amp; electrostatics</h2>
<p class="opk">One <code>squared_law</code> operator, two regimes: <code>law: gravity</code> (mass, always attract, all-pairs) collapses a disc into a galaxy; <code>law: coulomb</code> (signed charge, like-repel) is a plasma.</p>
<div class="sim-gallery">
  <figure class="sim-card">

# a rotating disc of stars collapses into arms.
config/inverse_square/spiral_galaxy.yaml</pre></span></span>
      <span class="sim-cap">squared_law (law: gravity) — a rotating disc collapses into a galaxy</span>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
</div>

<p class="opk">A single lateral operator rides a whole cloud along a dissipative 3D chaotic flow ẋ = f(x); a tiny seed is stretched-and-folded until the cloud <em>is</em> the attractor. Ten systems ship; four shown.</p>
```

## Differentiable optimization — a foraging colony

Because the whole rollout is differentiable, a *design* can be optimized, not just simulated.
A slime-style foraging colony (the same `deposit`/`diffuse`/`sense`/`glide` operators) is tuned
by a black-box UCB search over its spec parameters — from a hand-set start to the best found.
Each strip runs left → right, start → optimized.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
{{< video gallery/initial.mp4 title="initial hand-set colony" >}}

{{< video gallery/winner_7.mp4 title="optimized colony — ~5× faster to food" >}}
:::

The same recipe scales to harder navigation — a porous **pillar** field and a walled **maze**,
each crossed by a self-generated attractant gradient and tuned by the same optimizer:
